parameterBindings.derivation: the seed declares no default (50-f3j.json phases[1].validity.minRounds resolves through the parameter) and it is bound 1 before /prescribe-draw (CompetitionSetup). F3J.11 states no minimum number of fly-off rounds (F3J.11.1–F3J.11.4: organisation, 15-min working time, scoring as in F3J.10, final placing) and nothing through F3J.12 states one either — the rulebook's silence is a parameter, so 1 is the least-constraining rulebook-consistent choice (the ales ledger's minNewGroup=1 precedent). Never exercised on this pair — the fly-off never draws (16 qualifying rounds fill the window; phase 2's parameters are never reached).

metricMappings.mechanism: seed-declared whenNotRecorded (Number 0), resolved by the engine (FlightMetricResolution tier 1, metric-absence-semantics.md) — the harness emits NO assumed values; the capture map records only what the fixture data carries (the seed declares no lateLandingDeduction/launchHeight metrics, so the definition-gated arms capture nothing).
metricMappings.justification: P1 (assumed-clean unless recorded to the contrary): seconds past the working time are what the timekeeper records; a flight landing within time has none. F3J.10.3 — 'A penalty of thirty (30) points will be deducted from the flight score for overflying the end of the group's working time for up to a maximum of one (1) minute' — and F3J.10.4 — 'A zero score will be recorded for overflying the end of the group's working time by more than one (1) minute' — are the rulebook shape the seed's overflySeconds metric and its flightValidWhen gate implement. Corroborated inside the foil's own data: the longest decoded flight is 598 s, inside the 600 s working time (F3J.6.2 b), so no row could carry a positive value.

metricMappings.mechanism: seed-declared whenNotRecorded (Flag false), resolved by the engine — no harness-emitted values.
metricMappings.justification: P1: F3J.10.8 — 'the model aircraft touches either the competitor or his helper during the landing manoeuvre, no landing points will be given' — is an exception a helper records. No GS column records it on this fixture, so the benign value (no contact; the landing award stands) is the negative recording. The seed declares the flag inside the conditional gating its landing lookup (overflySeconds = 0 AND touchedByCompetitor = false).

metricMappings.mechanism: seed-declared whenNotRecorded (Flag true), resolved by the engine — no harness-emitted values.
metricMappings.justification: P1: F3J.5.1 e — 'The flight is cancelled and recorded as a zero score if, during landing, some part of the model aircraft does not come to rest within 75 metres of the centre of the competitor's designated landing circle' — is an exception a timer/helper records; an unrecorded cancellation is the negative recording of the exception. Corroborated inside the foil's own data: every scores-raw row carries LandingOver75m false (no contrary record). The seed declares the flag as the flightValidWhen gate, matching F3J.5.1 e's shape — it zeroes the flight, not the bonus.

excludedOracleCells.reason: D5 phantom group 5: GS's R1 export carries five all-zero placeholder rows (pilots 7, 11, 17, 39, 56 — oracle keys 1/1/5/0/{7,11,17,39,56}) whose pilots also fly real flights in groups 1/4 of the same round (fixture provenance.json: 'Round 1 carries a phantom group 5: five zero-score rows (pilots 7, 11, 17, 39, 56) whose pilots also have real flights in groups 1/4 of the same round; kept verbatim. GS aggregates best-per-original-round keeping the highest, so these rows do not alter totals or drops'). The draw derivation's dedup keeps each pilot's real flight (highest oracle NormalisedScore per (pilot, original round) — ReplayDriver.cs:1038-1049, matching GS's own best-per-original-round aggregation, which is what makes the phantom neutral) and drops the phantoms, so these 5 oracle cells are never replayed or compared. Declared scope in provenance (decision 7), never a triaged entry: a never-compared cell is not a difference.

notes: The story's original guaranteed-divergence claim — GS's local Drop1AtRound=8 forcing a drop-policy split — stands WITHDRAWN: GS DropScoreOption=0, Drop1AtRound=8 (competition.json scoring) equals the seed's phases[0].drops[0] applyWhenRoundsCompletedAtLeast: 8, and F3J.3.1 a — 'If more than seven qualification rounds are flown, then the lowest score will be discarded before determining the aggregate score' — makes 8 the rulebook threshold (16 scored rounds fire exactly one drop per pilot on both sides). The 20 ranking moves come from the score cells, not the drop policy; where the dropped cell sits differently on each side (pilot 12: R14 vs R1, pilot 25: R13 vs R1, pilot 26: R9 vs R14, pilot 54: R13 vs R7, pilot 2: R13 vs R16) that is a consequence of the cell differences below, never a policy difference.

The −30 payload is not mapped — the offences differ (decision 3): all 11 FlightScoreDeduction=30 rows carry flight times 182–596 s, inside the 600 s working time, so F3J.10.3's overfly offence (flying past the end of working time) cannot describe them; GS's durFlightPenalty=1 late-landing scheme (competition.json familyRows.Dur; provenance.json: '11 rows carry FlightScoreDeduction=30; Penalty is 0 everywhere') is a local GS construct the rulebook does not state. The harness captures nothing for the column under this seed — the capture gate reads the published definition (ReplayDriver.cs:1161-1168) and the seed declares no lateLandingDeduction metric — so the seed-run scores those rows +30 relative to GS. Triaged below, never reconciled.

Teams reach no persisted score: UseTeams=true with all 30 pilots assigned across 8 teams (sizes 4,3,4,4,4,3,4,4 — competition.json triageJustification.teams), but team standings are report-time aggregations of unchanged individual normalised scores, never an input to them; the parallel comparator's deliberate no-team-grain stance holds (the ales precedent).

GS re-rounds Score and RawScore to GroupScoreDecimals (1 dp, RoundOrTruncate=0 HalfUp) before comparing, then sorts Score DESC / RawScore DESC with ties displayed '=n' — the =n tie-display semantics vs the engine's exact-decimal ties. Inert on this pair: no aggregate ties exist on either side (every rank 1–30 is distinct on both sides), but the rounding grid's sub-0.1 shifts are exactly the kind of perturbation that could create or dissolve an '=n' display — a rounding-cascade disclosure, not a separate entry.

Unexercised parameters: flyoffSize is defaulted (9) — the defaulted arm binds nothing (christchurch decision-8 precedent) and the fly-off never draws; carryPenalties is unbound (decision 6 — a Flag bind would widen the decimal-typed bind pipeline for a parameter that is never read: the fly-off phase never draws, so promotion's CarryPenalties never resolves; F3J states nothing about carry-over); flyoffMinRounds is bound (1, above) but never read. Unbound-but-never-read is safe: the engine resolves parameters per use, and phase 2's parameters are never reached.

The R1 540 target is oracle-reconciled knowledge and is never bound under the seed (decision 4): the export carries no DurTargetTimeByRound rows at all (competition.json scheduleTables.DurTargetTimeByRound.rows is empty — ReplayDriver.cs:185-203) and 22 R1 flights over 540 s imply the target exactly (every decay witness solves T = (t + TS)/2 = 540); the fixture's RoundParameterBindings entry is parity-only and the parallel run refuses fixture round binds (ReplayDriver.cs:646-655), and the seed declares no targetTime parameter — nothing to bind. The decay difference is triaged below, never applied.

GS's landing-0 convention is generic, documented and code-verified — the club-convention reading of the 34 recorded 0.0s (no landing bonus; the pilot landed off the tape) is GliderScore's own explicit rule, not an inference: the Landings form prints 'The Landing Distance 0 is a special case and automatically receives 0 Points. Distance and/or Points entries of 0 or less will not be saved.' for EVERY landing table in the catalogue (gliderscore/GliderScore_Master/Lndgs_FRM.vb:296-298, set in the form's load handler); GetLandingBonus short-circuits before the exact-match lookup — If LndgDistance = 0 Then Return 0 (Scoring_MOD.vb:737-738); and GS injects a 0→0 row into every landing table at load (Comps1.vb:4586, GlobalFunctions_MOD.vb:1327 and :1413 — 'adds the record 0 distance = 0 points to the table'), which is exactly the fixture-authored class-definition.json's explicit upTo: 0 → 0 row cited in the sentinel entry below. This strengthens the sentinel's disclosure but does not change its triage: F3J.10.5's measurement semantics genuinely award 100 for a recorded 0.0 m nose-to-spot distance (its first band, 'up to 0.2'), so the collision — a recorded numeral overloaded between GS's program rule and the rulebook's table read literally — stands triaged kind 1, and the ending of that overload belongs to the declared-instrument model (tape-points-landing-seeds.md decision 8's three-way distinction: off-the-tape, 0 m on the spot, and no measurement).

Retriage 2026-09-28 (landing-zero-and-flyaway-encoding story): the seed's landing table gained a leading {upTo: 0, points: 0} convention row (SeedF3J.cs LandingRows — an exact 0 m reading is physically impossible, so exact 0 is reserved as paper 'beyond the tape' → zero landing points), the landing conditional gained a flightTime < 600 horn test, and the rate caps moved 600→599 (900→899 fly-off). On this pair only the zero row binds: the longest decoded flight is 598 s (noted above), so the 599 cap and the <600 test never engage, and the fly-off never draws (899 never read). Seed and GS now AGREE 0→0 on every pure Landing-0.0 cell — GS's own rule (previous note: Lndgs_FRM.vb:296-298, Scoring_MOD.vb:737-738, the injected 0→0 row) meeting the seed's new convention row — so the landing-0 sentinel raw class collapses and its ledger entry retires here (raw pin 54→32, normalised pin 264→232, fourteen ranking splits healed, six remain for their decay/deduction/rounding causes). Cells sharing the −30 deduction (11 rows) or the R1 decay (22 flights, R1G1P44 carrying both) still differ for those other reasons, triaged in their own entries. The previous note stands as the pre-story record.

triagedDifferences.difference: Raw score-cell −30 late-landing deduction: 11 rows carry FlightScoreDeduction=30 (R1G1P44, R5G4P7, R6G3P2, R6G4P63, R10G3P2, R12G2P63, R13G1P42, R13G4P54, R14G2P25, R14G3P44, R14G4P7), and GS deducts the payload from the raw pre-normalisation; the seed declares no such term, so the seed-run scores those rows +30 relative to GS. The offences differ: every deduction row sits inside the 600 s working time (flight times 182–596 s), so F3J.10.3's overfly offence cannot describe them, and GS's durFlightPenalty=1 late-landing scheme is a local GS construct the rulebook does not state — the payload is not mapped (decision 3: the mapping policy fixes values, not offences). The landing award on all eleven now agrees (every deduction row records Landing 0.0, and the seed's {0,0} convention row meets GS's 0→0 rule there — the retired sentinel's meeting point, provenance note 8): the gap is the deduction alone. Ten rows show raw deltas of exactly +30.0 in the comparator report; the eleventh, R1G1P44, additionally carries the R1 decay below (raw 596 vs 454.0, delta +142 = decay + deduction). Pinned raw-mismatch count: 32 across the two raw classes (this deduction and the R1 decay below) — the wildcard covers any cell, so the count is what makes the entry exact (decision 1).
triagedDifferences.citation: Rulebook: F3J.10.3 — 'A penalty of thirty (30) points will be deducted from the flight score for overflying the end of the group's working time for up to a maximum of one (1) minute' — the overfly offence, which the seed's conditional implements exactly (overflySeconds > 0 → −30) and which never fires here (overflySeconds unrecorded → 0, and no flight overflew). Local practice: competition.json familyRows.Dur.durFlightPenalty = 1 puts GS's late-landing scheme in force (provenance.json: 'durFlightPenalty=1 puts the late-landing deduction mode in force (unlike ales-sample-comp): 11 rows carry FlightScoreDeduction=30; Penalty is 0 everywhere'); the capture gate reads the published definition — the seed class in parallel-run mode (ReplayDriver.cs:1161-1168) — and the seed declares no lateLandingDeduction metric, so the harness captures nothing for the column. Triage kind 1 — local variation: the offences differ, so the payload is disclosed and never reconciled (decision 3).

triagedDifferences.difference: Raw score-cell R1 over-target decay: GS scored round 1 against a 540 s target with linear over-target decay (target − (t − target)), while rounds 2–16 held the 600 s target with no decay; 22 R1 flights over 540 s witness it (every one solves T = (t + TS)/2 = 540 exactly — oracle-reconciled, the export carrying no DurTargetTimeByRound rows, ReplayDriver.cs:185-203). The seed's working time is a fixed 600 s with a 1 pt/s rate term capped PerFlight at 599 and no decay clause, so the seed-run scores those 22 flights at their flight time — up to 114 points above GS's decayed value (R1G2P62: seed 694 vs GS 580.0; his recorded 0.8 m landing agrees on both sides). Two of the 22 record Landing 0.0 (R1G3P13 and R1G1P44 — the retired sentinel's last shared cells): the landing award now agrees 0→0 there and their deltas (+110 and +142) are decay alone, plus the −30 deduction for P44 (entry above). The 599 cap never binds on this pair (longest decoded flight 598 s).
triagedDifferences.citation: Rulebook: F3J.6.2 b — 'The working time allowed to each competitor in a group shall be of exactly ten (10) minutes duration' — the fixed 600 s the seed's timing declares; F3J.10.1 c ends the timed attempt at 'completion of the group's working time', so no flight scores beyond 600 s (the seed's rate term caps PerFlight at 599 (landing-zero story; inert here — longest decoded flight 598 s); the 1 pt/s rate itself is the universal F3J convention, carried at docs/rules/f3j.md:74-78 as convention, not citation). The rulebook states no over-target decay clause. Local practice: GS scored R1 against 540 s (competition.json familyRows.Dur.durTargetTime 600 covers rounds 2–16; the R1 value exists nowhere in the fixture's input files — DurTargetTimeByRound has zero rows — and is oracle-reconciled in the parity harness, ReplayDriver.cs:185-203, never bound under the seed: decision 4). Triage kind 1 — local variation: correct on both sides.

Witnessed on 200 cells with identical raws and unshifted group maxima — the first sighting on the corpus of the HalfUp-vs-Truncate split. Witness cell 1/1/4/0/11: exact 1000·421/588 = 715.986… → GS 716.0 vs seed 715.9. triagedDifferences.citation: Rulebook: F3J.10.11 — 'The corrected score shall be recorded (truncated) to one place after the decimal point' — truncation is the cited rulebook position, implemented by 50-f3j.json's normalise.round (Truncate, 0.1). Local practice: the club's GS grid rounds HalfUp to 1 dp (competition.json scoring: GroupScoreDecimals 1, RoundOrTruncate 0) — the same grid the christchurch pair witnessed where the rulebook was silent; here the rulebook speaks and the citation is stronger. Triage kind 1 — local variation: correct on both sides.

triagedDifferences.difference: Normalised-cell composition/renormalisation cascade: the 32 non-rounding normalised mismatches — 31 cells carrying their own raw mismatch (21 R1 decay cells and the 10 deduction rows outside R1; R1G1P44's R1 cell carries both) plus 1 raw-unchanged rescaled cell (R1G1P25: raw agrees both sides, seed 629.7 vs GS 732.2, −102.5 — the R1G1 max raw moved 590 → 686). The group max moved in exactly 3 groups, all round 1: R1G1 (GS winner p49 alone at 1000 — the only R1G1 cell absent from the normalised report, so GS's 1000 — vs seed co-winners p29+p49, p49 agreeing at the top on both sides while p29's decayed raw joins him; every other R1G1 mismatch carries its own raw), R1G2 (winner p32 at GS 1000.0 → p62 at seed 1000; all 7 mismatches carry their own raw) and R1G3 (winner p50 at GS 1000.0 → p26 at seed 1000; all 8 carry their own raw). In the ten deduction groups (R5G4, R6G3, R6G4, R10G3, R12G2, R13G1, R13G4, R14G2, R14G3, R14G4) the maxima hold — each group's sole non-rounding cell carries its own +30 raw (deltas +43.0…+43.5) with no winner-change row. R13G3 rejoins the agreeing set: its old +100 sentinel raw now agrees and its sole mismatch is R13G3P32 rounding (−0.1). Cites the two raw classes as its causes; the remaining 200 normalised mismatches are the rounding grid (the entry above).
triagedDifferences.citation: Rulebook: F3J.10.10 — the group winner is 'the highest aggregate of points comprising of flight points plus landing bonus points minus penalty points' — the composition whose seed-side value the two raw classes change; F3J.10.11 — each competitor's corrected score is his own score 'multiplied by 1000 / highest points total scored in the group before correction' — the renormalisation that propagates a moved max to every raw-unchanged cell. Local practice causes: the R1 540 s decay (22 flights) and the −30 late-landing deduction (11 rows, GS-side only) — each triaged above. The retired landing-0 sentinel (provenance note 8) causes none of the 32. Triage kind 1 — local variation: correct on both sides.
